content.title: Today is the day Artemis II comes... - From Quarks to Quasars | Facebook
content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?From Quarks to Quasars's PostFrom Quarks to Quasars6d · Shared with PublicToday is the day Artemis II comes home.After a 10-day, 425,000-mile (685,000 km) journey around the Moon, the Orion spacecraft is set to splash down in the Pacific Ocean today — marking the end of the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years.Splashdown is scheduled for 5:07 p.m. PT (8:07 p.m. ET) today. That’s 1:07 a.m. GMT (April 11), 2:07 a.m. in Central Europe, and 10:07 a.m. in Sydney, Australia.And yes — it will be streamed live.As Orion re-enters Earth’s atmosphere at around 25,000 miles per hour (40,000 km/h), it will streak across the sky like a fireball before deploying parachutes and descending into the ocean near San Diego, California.The final phase takes about 13 minutes, including a brief communications blackout as the spacecraft passes through superheated plasma.Then come the parachutes — and finally, splashdown.After traveling farther than any humans since 1970, the crew’s journey ends not on a runway, but in the open ocean, watched in real time by the world.Stay tuned for updates!Learn more: "Artemis II splashdown in California visual guide, what it would look like."
